hero.lead: A nation of 64.7 million that issued the world’s first wildlife conservation bond, and still makes more than nine-tenths of its electricity from non-renewable sources, most of it coal.

capital.heading: 4 instruments. A rhino bond, a transition partnership and two World Bank loans.

record.text: Just Energy Transition Partnership: Initial mobilisation; the plan identifies $98 billion of needs over five years
Sustainable and Low-Carbon Energy Transition Development Policy Loan: Budget support for energy reform
Eskom Just Energy Transition Project: Repurposing a coal plant
Wildlife Conservation Bond: Success payment up to $13.76m, tied to black rhino population growth

register.name: Sustainable and Low-Carbon Energy Transition Development Policy Loan
register.text: Supports reforms that open the power sector and lower its emissions.

register.name: Eskom Just Energy Transition Project
register.text: Finances the decommissioning and repurposing of a coal plant, with support for workers and communities.

register.name: Wildlife Conservation Bond
register.detail: Issued 23 March 2022 · Outcome bond, matures 31 March 2027
register.note: Success payment up to $13.76m, tied to black rhino population growth
register.text: Investors forgo coupons. At maturity they receive a success payment if rhino numbers grow in Addo Elephant National Park and the Great Fish River Nature Reserve, funded by a grant from the Global Environment Facility.

register.name: Just Energy Transition Partnership
register.detail: Investment plan published 7 November 2022 · Partnership finance
register.note: Initial mobilisation; the plan identifies $98 billion of needs over five years
register.text: Finance from France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the United States and the European Union for the first phase of the shift away from coal.
